Role of polylactic acid microplastics during anaerobic co-digestion of cow 
manure and Chinese cabbage waste enhanced by nanobubble

A B S T R A C T
With the increasing use of plastic products globally, environmental pollution by plastic waste is becoming 
increasingly problematic. This study investigated the impacts of two types of polylactic acid microplastics, clear 
microplastics and aluminised film microplastics, on methane yield, microbial community, and volatile fatty acid 
accumulation during anaerobic co-digestion of cow manure and Chinese cabbage waste under different tem­
perature conditions. The influence of the addition of air nanobubbles on microplastic degradation in the 
anaerobic digestion system we also examined. The results revealed that under thermophilic conditions, clear and 
aluminised film microplastics increased the methane yield, with the latter resulting in greater improvement. 
Conversely, under mesophilic conditions, the presence of microplastics reduced the methane yield, but the 
addition of air-nanobubble partially mitigated this effect. Microplastics also affected the microbial community, 
with specific species showing correlations with methane yield. Methanothermobacter, which is linked to lactic 
acid conversion, was positively correlated with methane yield, whereas Methanomassiliicoccus levels increased in 
the presence of microplastics, particularly in the inhibited state of the digester. These results suggest that, under 
thermophilic conditions, microplastics may increase the cumulative methane yield by facilitating the

1. Introduction
Co-digestion of cow manure (CM) and Chinese cabbage waste (CCW) 
can increase anaerobic digestion (AD) system stability and methane 
yield by encouraging microbial diversity and synergistic effects (Liu 
et al., 2022). AD efficiency is strongly influenced by the makeup of CM 
and CCW, which may contain a high proportion of difficult-to-degrade 
substances or form toxic compounds (Zhang et al., 2024).
In addition, plastics are increasingly used globally and the fact that 
many agricultural services are provided by plastics (Liu et al., 2014), 
some of which degrade into microplastics (MPs) over time because of 
physical, chemical and biological reactions. These MPs subsequently 
find their way into livestock waste through processes such as animal 
feeding, manure composting, and other means (Wu et al., 2021a,b; 
Zhang et al., 2020). MPs are plastic fragments and particles with a 
diameter of less than 5 mm The biofilms present on MPs can serve as 
carriers for pathogens and may also adsorb heavy metals (Lu et al., 
2020). Fecal matter containing MPs can introduce these harmful sub­
stances into farmlands, which in turn have the potential to enter the 
human body via crops or other pathways, thereby posing a threat to 
human health (Lu et al., 2020). MPs were detected in CM at an abun­
dance of 74 items per kilogram of wet matter (Sheriff et al., 2023).
MPs may adversely affect AD under short-term and long-term 
exposure, and different MPs may affect AD depending on their phys­
ical and chemical properties (Mohammad Mirsoleimani Azizi et al., 
2021). Petroleum-based plastics such as polyvinyl chloride MPs (50 nm) 
inhibit methane yield by hindering acid production during AD. They 
also induce oxidative stress, which reduces cell viability (Wang et al., 
2022a). Polyethylene MPs can inhibit diversity and affect interspecies 
electron transfer and related genes in methanogens, attenuating related 
enzymes and electron transfer activities, and further reducing methane 
yield rates (Wang et al., 2022b). Howere, biobased plastics such as 
polylactic acid plastic (PLA), which is derived from the fermentation of 
starch or sugarcane and has excellent degradation properties, utilised 
thermophilic methanogens under thermophilic conditions to degrade 
lactic acid polypeptides while completing the methane conversion, 
which can promote methane yield (Bandini, 2020; Shang et al., 2023). 
However, PLA degradation under mesophilic conditions is different 
from that under thermophilic conditions, and the PLA copolymer can be 
completely degraded in 116 ± 48 days at 55 ◦C and in 423 ± 76 days at 
37 ◦C (Cazaudehore et al., 2021; Lu et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2018).
Biodegradable plastics are used as alternatives to traditional fossil- 
source plastics because of their biodegradability under specific condi­
tions (Peng et al., 2024). PLA is the world’s highest-capacity bioplastic, 
accounting for 31.0% of bioplastic capacity and is expected to account 
for 43.6% by 2028 (EUBP, 2023). PLA is used in a wide range of ap­
plications such as product packaging, construction, and agriculture 
(Jamshidian et al., 2010). PLA in practical applications, to cater to the 
characteristics required by the market, is usually further processed 
(Jamshidian et al., 2010). In agricultural production, aluminised mulch 
is widely used for pest control (Croxton and Stansly, 2014), so it often 
appears in agricultural waste and ends up in livestock manure (Li et al., 
2014). Aluminised films use the excellent physicochemical properties of 
aluminium to enhance the barrier properties, light reflection properties 
and antistatic capabilities of plastic films, thereby improving their 
functionality (Mwema et al., 2018). With the gradual and widespread 
use of PLA, the prospect of aluminised films on PLA surfaces, such as 
aluminised PLA mulch, which has a high probability of appearing in 
agricultural waste, livestock manure, etc., will be very wide.
Therefore, simple, economical, and efficient methods are needed to 
reduce the negative impact of PLA-MPs on AD while improving 
hydrolysis and stabilising the digester during AD. Nanobubbles (NBs) 
can improve substrate accessibility, digestibility and enzyme activity 
due to their small size, high electrostatic interactions and ability to 
generate reactive oxygen species (Chuenchart et al., 2021). Therefore, 
the addition of nanobubble water (NBW) to AD to facilitate the 
resourceful utilisation of substrates has gradually gained attention. The 
addition of NBW increased the hydrolysis and acidification processes of 
AD, and the reactive oxygen species generated by NBW promoted the 
hydrolysis of lignin by breaking its encapsulated structure, which 
increased the degradation rate of lignin by 19.0%, and simultaneously 
increased the abundance of hydrolysing bacteria and methanogens by 
52.9% and 63.8%, respectively (Yang et al., 2020). NBW can increase 
water mobility, allowing more nutrients to be transferred to microbial 
cells and increasing the production of extracellular enzymes, which in­
crease the activity of extracellular hydrolytic enzymes by 14.0%–17.0% 
and those related to lignocellulose decomposition by 38.0% (Wang 
et al., 2020). NBW creates a trace amount of oxygen to increase the 
efficiency of the electron transport system by a factor of 1.7, resulting in 
a VFA (Volatile Fatty Acid) reduction of 193 NmL g−1VS by enhancing 
the activity of parthenogenetic bacteria (Wang et al., 2021a). Among the 
multiple types of NBW (air, CO2, He and N2), air-NBW is the most 
cost-effective, increasing proteolysis and resulting in a 27.8% increase in 
the cumulative methane yield (Wang et al., 2024). In addition, the 
combination of MPs and NBs resulted in an increase in the measured 
mean particle size and concentration, while the NBs decreased the ag­
gregation between MPs, and the presence of NBs bound to MPs made 
them more stable in the anaerobic environment (Wang et al., 2023). 
However, studies of NBW and MPs acting together in AD are more 
limited, and questions about whether NBW or MPs have a greater effect 
on AD, and whether the simultaneous presence of NBW and MPs affects 
AD differently are currently unknown. Additionally, how biobased MPs 
promote or hinder AD is insufficiently studied, and how to amplify their 
promoting effect or alleviate their hindering effect is unclear.
Therefore, this study focuses on clear PLA (CP) and aluminised film 
PLA (AP) as representatives to explore how the presence of biobased 
MPs affects AD during anaerobic co-digestion of CM and CCW, and 
whether the facilitation of AD by NBW is affected by the presence of 
PLA-MPs. To assess the stability of AD, the pH, soluble chemical oxygen 
demand (SCOD), volatile fatty acid (VFA), total ammonia nitrogen 
(TAN), and CMY of the AD system were determined in this study.
2. Materials and methods
2.1. Preparation of NBW
The air-NBW used in this study was prepared via a nanobubble 
generator (JXWNP-AL01, Jinxiang, China). Air was introduced into 
deionized water (DW) through this generator for 20 min at 20 ± 2 ◦C 
and left for 10 min to change the liquid from milky to clear to obtain the 
NBW for the whole AD process. The pressure of the nanobubble gener­
ator was controlled between 0.4 and 0.5 MPa during the preparation of 
NBW. After preparation, NBW was used in the subsequent AD.
2.2. Materials
CM and CCW were collected from a dairy farm and wholesale 
vegetable market in Lanzhou, China. There are two types of PLA plastic: 
CP and AP. CP is a film with a thickness of 25 μm and a smooth surface, 
and the AP is a film with a thickness of 0.1 nm that is plated on CP via a 
vacuum single-sided aluminising method. According to the measure­
ment, the conductivity of the aluminised film is 2991.5 S m−1, which is

electrically conductive (ST2253y, Suzhou, China). PLA is purchased 
from Huixing Environmental Protective Material Co., Ltd. (China). In 
the laboratory, circles with a diameter of 1.5 ± 0.1 mm were cut via a 
1.5 mm hole punch (4120, Tianhong, China) (Lu et al., 2022). CM and 
CCW were crushed with a pulveriser and stored at 4 ± 1 ◦C in advance. 
The inoculums used in the experiment were domesticated thermophilic 
and mesophilic digested sludge. The Supplementary material section 
lists the major characteristics of the different substrates used in this 
study.
2.3. Experimental design
The experimental setup and sampling methods were similar to those 
used in previous experiments (Liu et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2024). A 
digester with a working volume of 1 L was used; on the basis of previous 
experiments, the optimal substrate mixing ratio was selected. The 
optimal substrate ratio with the best hydrolysis effect and higher 
methane yield efficiency, CM:CCW = 1:1 (wet basis) (Liu et al., 2022), 
for the best hydrolysis and higher methane yield efficiency in general 
was selected, whereas the substrate (CM + CCW) and water ratio = 1:1 
(Zhang et al., 2024) were chosen on the basis of the optimal total solids 
(TS) for AD, resulting in a TS of approximately 10% for the reactor (Abid 
et al., 2021). A total of 700 g of CM, CCW and water was finally loaded. 
Equal amounts of CP and AP were added to the anaerobic digester mixed 
with NBW or DW at a concentration of 5.0 ± 0.1 g Kg−1TS, respectively. 
The concentration of MPs was referenced from Lu et al. (2022), which 
was a minimum concentration of MPs close to the range of the global 
level (It¨avaara et al., 2002). This experiment uses two temperatures, 
thermophilic (T, 55 ± 1 ◦C) and mesophilic (M, 37 ± 1 ◦C), with a total 
of ten conditions, which are TD (T + DW), TDCP (T + DW + CP), TDAP 
(T + DW + AP), TNCP (T + NBW + CP), TNAP (T + NBW + AP), MD (M 
+ DW), MDCP (M + DW + CP), MDAP (M + DW + AP), MNCP (M +
NBW + CP), and MNAP (M + NBW + AP). Details are provided in 
Table 1, where TD and MD served as the control group. Subsequently, 
70 g of thermophilic or mesophilic seed sludge was added to the di­
gesters. Three sets of parallel experiments were set up for each set. A 
portion of the digestion mixture was pumped out by a peristaltic pump 
at the same weekly intervals and centrifuged at 2000 g for 5 min. The 
supernatant was removed and filtered through a 0.45 μm polyether 
sulfone microfibre filter, and the filtered liquid was used for experi­
mental testing. The pH was not artificially adjusted in this study.
2.4. Analytical methods
TS, volatile solids (VS), pH, TAN, SCOD, and total alkalinity (TA) 
were determined via the standard method (APHA, 1998). The free 
ammonia nitrogen (FAN) content was calculated via the equation pro­
vided by Hansen et al. (1998). The VFA was determined via a gas 
chromatograph (SP-7890 Plus, Ruihong, China) with an organic acid 
analytical column (320 μm inner diameter, 0.50 μm film, and 30 m total 
length) and a flame ionization detector. The volume of biogas was 
measured via a gas flowmeter (LML-2, Alpha, China), and the methane 
concentration in the biogas was measured via a biogas composition 
analyser (GA5000, Geotach, United Kingdom).
Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) extraction was performed at fixed 
times, and the microbial community was analysed by sequencing the 
V3–V4 and V4–V5 hypervariable regions of the 16S rDNA gene. Bacteria 
were amplified with primers 341F (CCTACGGGGNGGCWGCAG) and 
806R (GGACTACHVGGGGTATCTAAT), and archaea were amplified 
with primers Arch519F (CAGCMGCCGCGGGTAA) and Arch915R 
(GTGCTCCCCCGCCAATTCCT). Sequencing was then performed on the 
Illumina MiSeq platform (AxyPrep DNA Gel Extraction Kit, Axygen 
Biosciences, Union City, CA, U.S.), and microbial abundance and ty­
pology analyses were conducted to determine differences in the micro­
bial community in each digester.
2.5. Statistical analysis
In this study, all the statistical analyses were performed via SPSS 
27.0 version software for Windows. One-way ANOVA was used to 
evaluate the effects of different experimental conditions on the outcome 
variables. Duncan’s Multiple Range Test, T-test and Dunnett’s T3 test 
were used to determine the differences between the different samples 
with a confidence level of 95%. The data are shown as the means ±
standard deviations. P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant (Lu 
et al., 2022). CMY was fitted using a modified Gompertz model (Liu 
et al., 2022).
3. Results and discussion
3.1. Digestion performance
3.1.1. Characteristics of the digestate
The pH (Fig. 1a and b) is an essential indicator of AD, and a suitable 
pH for methanogens is in the range of 6.5–8.0 (Li et al., 2017). During 
AD, the pH under thermophilic conditions was greater than that under 
mesophilic conditions, probably because temperature affects microbial 
processes by influencing the nature of metabolism, nutrient re­
quirements, biomass composition, and reaction rates (Maleki et al., 
2018). Thermophilic conditions promote hydrolysis, which breaks down 
VFA in time and does not result in the accumulation of VFA (Li et al., 
2023; Zhang et al., 2024). The pH slightly decreased in the initial stage, 
probably because PLA was hydrolysed as a substrate to produce VFA 
when it was added to the AD digester, which led to an increase in VFA 
and a decrease in pH (Seeley et al., 2020). However, the pH under 
mesophilic conditions decreased more than that under thermophilic 
conditions in the initial stage, probably because acid-producing bacteria 
adapt to the environment faster than methanogens do and grow faster 
resulting in the accumulation of VFA from PLA (Clagnan et al., 2023). In 
addition to VFA, pH is also affected by the amount of ammonia present 
in the digester (Wang et al., 2024).
Ammonia is usually produced by the hydrolysis of proteinaceous 
substances in the substrate (Liu et al., 2022). A reasonable concentration 
of ammonia can act as a buffer and provide nutrients for microorganisms 
(Zhang et al., 2024). Under thermophilic and mesophilic conditions, 
TAN (Fig. 1c and d) and FAN (see supplementary material) gradually 
increased during the digestion process. The activity of methanogens was 
significantly inhibited when the TAN was greater than 1500 mg L−1 or 
the FAN was greater than 250 mg L−1 (Liu et al., 2022). FAN is more 
toxic to methanogens than TAN, and FAN can penetrate microbial cell 
membranes and destroy enzyme systems (Liu et al., 2022). The TAN and 
FAN in the thermophilic digester were significantly greater than those in

At the end of the digestion process, the TAN and FAN in the NBW- 
unadded but PLA-added digesters were lower than those in the control 
group, suggesting that the addition of PLA-MPs may have affected the 
hydrolysis of AD to be negatively and that the addition of MPs caused 
the gene expression of hydrolysis-associated microorganisms to be 
impeded (Wang et al., 2022b). In contrast, the digesters with the addi­
tion of NBW presented higher TAN than the control group, and the TNCP 
and TNAP increased by 4.1% and 5.8%, respectively. The TAN of TNCP 
and TNAP were significantly greater than that of TD on Day 7 (P < 0.01), 
with increases of 6.0% and 8.2%, respectively. These findings indicate 
that, in addition to temperature, NBW also plays a role in protein hy­
drolysis (Zhang et al., 2024). The promotion of AD hydrolysis by NBW 
was greater than the hindering effect of MPs, and the presence of MPs 
did not affect the NBW promotion of the hydrolysis stage. TAN shows an 
increasing trend, in contrast to SCOD, which usually shows an overall 
increasing and then decreasing trend (Wang et al., 2024).
SCOD (Fig. 1e and f) is an essential indicator of the amount of dis­
solved reducing substances in the digestate (Liu et al., 2022). On Day 3, 
SCOD peaked under thermophilic and mesophilic conditions. Never­
theless, the SCOD level under thermophilic conditions was significantly 
greater than that under mesophilic conditions (P < 0.01), and the TD 
was 23.5% greater than that under MD, which might be due to the 
complete hydrolysis and release of more VFA under thermophilic 
conditions.
Under thermophilic conditions, SCOD levels peaked on Day 3. The 
SCOD level of TD was the greatest and the TDAP level was the lowest, 
the TDAP level was 14.3% lower than that of TD, and there was a sig­
nificant difference (P < 0.01). It is speculated that the AD reactor was 
already in the methanogenic stage at this time, and SCOD had begun to 
decline before sampling. This finding also suggest that the addition of AP 
increased the suitability of methanogens for growth in the digester 
(Liang et al., 2023), therefore, the SCOD level decreased the fastest. 
Under mesophilic conditions, at the peak on Day 3, the SCOD levels were 
MNCP, MDCP, MDAP, MD, and MNAP in descending order. The SCOD 
level of the CP-added digesters were significantly greater than that of the 
AP-added digesters and significantly greater than that of the control 
digesters (P < 0.01), suggesting that the CP promoted hydrolysis, 
perhaps because CP was used as a substrate hydrolysed to increase the 
VFA in the system, whereas the aluminised film on the surface of the PLA 
physically impeded the hydrolysis of the PLA (Cazaudehore et al., 2022), 
resulting in the failure of the VFA release.
In general, VFA (Fig. 2), as a major component of SCOD, is a product 
of hydrolysis and acidification and is an essential intermediate during 
the AD (Li et al., 2017). On Day 3, the VFA levels of the TDCP and TNCP 
digesters were 12.9% and 21.2% greater than those of the control group, 
respectively. It can be assumed that CP was hydrolysed as additional 
carbonaceous organic matter in AD to produce more VFA (Seeley et al., 
2020). In contrast, the VFA levels of TDAP and TNAP were 15.0% and 
10.2% lower than those of TDCP and TNCP, respectively, suggesting that 
the methanogens grew more appropriately in the AP-added digester. 
During AD, the aluminised film of PLA was shed as PLA underwent 
hydrolysis because of its inherent conductivity, and the fallen 
aluminium functioned as the conductive material. Conductive materials 
promote the growth of bacteria by increasing the specific surface area 
and promoting the conversion of VFA by methanogens by enhancing the 
interspecies electron transfer (Liang et al., 2023). Furthermore, the VFA 
levels in the NBW-added digester were 12.4%–18.7% greater than those 
in the DW-added digester, which indicates that the addition of NBW 
leads to more efficient hydrolysis in the reaction, more complete sub­
strate degradation, and faster conversion of VFAs to methane (Zhang 
et al., 2024). This phenomenon is consistent with the results of subse­
quent studies (Fig. 3 and Table 2). It is speculated that the trace oxygen 
environment created by air-NBW promotes the expression of 
hydrolysis-associated parthenogenetic bacterial genes, thus allowing for 
an increase in VFA production from hydrolysis (Chuenchart et al., 
2021).
Under mesophilic conditions, the VFA levels of the MPs-added 
digester were greater than those of the control group, suggesting that 
the unhydrolysed MPs provided a greater specific surface area for the 
microbes to survive at a physical level, which allowed the more adapt­
able acid-producing bacteria to multiply faster, resulting in the

accumulation of VFA (Clagnan et al., 2023; Lee et al., 2022). The VFA 
level of MNAP was 3.2% greater than that of MDAP, so it was speculated 
that the hindering effect of AP on AD was less than the promoting effect 
of NBW, and that while AP provided the specific surface area for the 
microorganisms, NBW promoted hydrolysis to produce VFA either by 
increasing the mobility of water or by increasing the activity of hydro­
lytic enzymes (Chuenchart et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2024). The VFA 
levels were lower on Day 7 than on Day 3. The VFA levels in the 
AP-added digester decreased even further, indicating that the alumi­
nised film promoted the methane yield. The addition of aluminium can 
promote direct interspecies electron transfer between fermentative 
bacteria and methanogens, playing a positive role in maintaining the 
stability of the AD system and increasing the rate of methane yield, 
accelerating the process of converting accumulated VFA by metha­
nogens (Liang et al., 2023).
In addition, the VFA levels in the digesters with PLA and NBW were 
greater than those in the digester with only PLA, suggesting that NBW 
can promote hydrolysis and acidification (He et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 
2024). Nevertheless, the VFA in thermophilic and mesophilic digesters 
during AD were lower than those reported in the last survey (Liu et al., 
2022). This may be due to the different natures of the AD substrates and 
the influence of PLA on the AD (Fan et al., 2020; Li et al., 2017; Liu et al., 
2022).
3.1.2. Methane yields
The CMY was fitted with a modified Gompertz model (Fig. 3 and 
Table 2) to obtain the ultimate methane yield (UMY). The CMY (Fig. 3a 
and b) and daily methane yield rate (Fig. 3c and d) under thermophilic 
conditions were significantly higher than those under mesophilic con­
ditions (P < 0.01) because thermophilic conditions promoted hydrolysis 
during AD, which resulted in the complete hydrolysis of the substrate, 
greater utilisation of organic matter than that under mesophilic condi­
tions, and an increase in microbial activity, which offset the greater 
toxicity of FAN because of the increase in temperature (Liu et al., 2022). 
The fitting results revealed that the lag phase (λ) under thermophilic 
conditions was significantly smaller than that under mesophilic condi­
tions (P < 0.01), suggesting that thermophilic conditions increased the 
solubility of organic matter, accelerated biological and chemical pro­
cesses, and reduced the residence time (Fan et al., 2021).
Under thermophilic conditions, TNAP, TDAP, TDCP, and TNCP 
produced 18.3%, 16.4%, 10.6%, and 6.2% more methane than TD did, 
respectively, and TNAP and TDAP significantly increased in CMY 
compared with the TD (P < 0.01).
Compared with the control digester, the digester containing PLA- 
MPs produced more methane. PLA-MPs can be hydrolysed into lactic 
acid molecules as organic carbon substrates in AD, which leads to a yield 
of biomethane and improves the CMY (Clagnan et al., 2023). In addition, 
the CMY in the AP-added digester was greater than that in the CP-added 
digester, suggesting that not only the MPs but also the aluminised film 
on the MPs played a role in CMY in the AP-added digester. It can be 
assumed that the aluminised film is a type of conductive material that 
enhances AD through the following mechanisms: (1) it promotes direct 
interspecies electron transfer between substrate-oxidizing bacteria and 
methanogens, thus accelerating the CMY process (Yu et al., 2022); (2) it 
provides a high specific surface area to promote cell attachment and 
bacterial colonisation, thus increasing cell activity (Liang et al., 2023); 
(3) it enhances buffering capacity and lowers the oxidation-reduction 
potential (Wu et al., 2020); and (4) the aluminised film physically pre­
vents PLA from being completely hydrolysed, so the hydrophobic sur­
face of PLA can aid in AD by adsorbing and retaining lipids and other 
hydrophobic compounds, leading to better microbial metabolism and 
therefore more CMY (Lee et al., 2022). Therefore, the TNAP group had 
the maximum CMY. However, the effect of NBW on methanogens under 
thermophilic conditions did not show a clear pattern, and it was 
hypothesised that the promotion of AD methanogens by temperature 
was much greater than that of NBW, and that high temperature was the 
most important factor promoting methanogens under thermophilic 
conditions (Wang et al., 2022b). It is also possible that the thermophilic 
conditions caused the NBs to break easily, and the dissolution efficiency 
was reduced, which prevented the NBW from playing a role (Chuenchart 
et al., 2021).
Under mesophilic conditions, the CMY of MNCP was 11.6% greater 
than that of MD. The CMY of MDAP, MNAP, and MDCP were 22.3%, 
12.6%, and 0.1% lower, respectively, than that of MD, with MNCP 
showing a significant increase (P < 0.01) in CMY compared with MD, 
and MDAP showed a significant decrease (P < 0.01) in CMY compared 
with MD.
The CMY of the MPs-added digester was lower than that of the 
control group, which may be attributed to the following reasons: (1) PLA 
is resistant to AD (Cazaudehore et al., 2022) and cannot be fully

hydrolysed under mesophilic conditions (Nie et al., 2024), which 
physically prevents microbes from entering a suitable environment to 
grow and metabolise (Lee et al., 2022); (2) the addition of MPs can 
reduce the extracellular polymer content of the sludge, while the 
reduction in extracellular polymers weakens the extracellular electron 
transfer process, reducing the methane yield (Hou et al., 2020; Tang 
et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2022b). The AP-added digester had less CMY 
than the CP-added digester, because aluminium as an outer coating, 
does not easily decompose into small particles and detach from the PLA 
plastic at 37 ◦C (Mwema et al., 2018). The aluminium film envelops the 
PLA plastic, preventing it from fully contacting the substrate and making 
it difficult for microorganisms to adhere to the PLA plastic for decom­
position. Therefore, the aluminised film has a significant inhibitory ef­
fect on the hydrolysis of PLA under mesophilic conditions. In addition, 
the CMY was enhanced after the addition of NBW. It is speculated that 
the trace amount of oxygen generated by air-NBW promotes the hy­
drolysis of substrates in the acidification stage (Zhang et al., 2024), thus 
counteracting some of the resistance of PLA to AD under mesophilic 
conditions. The CMY in the MNCP group was the greatest as it was even 
more extensive than that in the control group. The rate of increase in 
CMY in the hydrolysis stage, from Day 5 to Day 9, of MNCP (Fig. 3d) was 
greater than that of all the other experimental groups. The MNCP was

3.2. Characteristics of the microbial community
3.2.1. Dominant bacterial community
The relative abundance (RA) of bacteria is affected by temperature, 
MPs and NBW (Fig. 4). The RA of some bacteria, such as Proteiniphilum 
and UCG-004, was reduced under the influence of MPs on Day 7. The 
addition of MPs significantly reduces the extracellular polymer content 
of anaerobic granular sludge, and increased levels of MPs lead to de­
creases in the nucleic acid, polysaccharide, and protein levels (Wang 
et al., 2022b). Proteiniphilum is responsible for polysaccharide hydroly­
sis, especially the hydrolysis of cellulose and xylan (Wu et al., 2021b). 
Proteiniphilum has many types of sugar-degrading enzymes, including 
glycoside hydrolases, carbohydrate esterases, and substrate-specific 
carbohydrate-binding motifs (Basak et al., 2022) and shows a signifi­
cant positive correlation with VFA levels (P < 0.01) (see the Supple­
mentary material section). Therefore, the bacterial RA responsible for 
polysaccharide hydrolysis was reduced by the addition of MPs.
RA was elevated in some bacteria under the influence of MPs, such as 
Ruminofilibacter, Herbinix, Defluviitalea, Hungateiclostridium saccincola, 
Caldicoprobacter, and LNR A2-18. Except for Defluviitalea and LNR A2- 
18, the remaining four bacterial genus were more enriched in the CP- 
added group. Ruminofilibacter has hemicellulose activity to degrade 
hemicellulose, and its activity increases after cellulose hydrolysis to 
release hemicellulose (Yang et al., 2023). Therefore, hemicellulose is 
more likely to appear in the stage after hydrolytic acidification, resulting 
in increased RA in the later stage. The average RA on Day 21 was 50.5% 
greater than that on Day 7 and was negatively correlated with the SCOD 
level (P < 0.05). Herbinix is a thermophilic bacterium that can degrade 
lignocellulose and hemicellulose, produce VFA (Beri et al., 2020) and 
can promote the hydrolysis of cellulose and the acid production of 
organic matter (Wang et al., 2021b). Therefore, the RA in the late stage 
was 57.1% lower than that in the early stage, which was positively

Defluviitalea was 97.1% greater in the early stage than in the late stage, 
showing a positive trend (P < 0.05) with SCOD. Under thermophilic 
conditions, the RA was 4.0%–5.0% greater with the CP-added digester 
than in the control group, which shows that CP can be considered to be 
externally added macromolecular organic matter under thermophilic 
conditions. AP-added digesters have a relatively high RA under ther­
mophilic conditions, suggesting that the added conductive layer pro­
motes the degradation of macromolecular organic matter, possibly 
because its conductivity facilitates interspecies electron transfer (Yu 
et al., 2022). Additionally, in mesophilic digesters with added CP, the 
RA of Defluviitalea increases, whereas in mesophilic digesters with added 
AP, the RA of Defluviitalea decreases. This suggests that under meso­
philic conditions, CP undergoes slight degradation, whereas AP becomes 
a barrier to the degradation of macromolecular organic matter. There­
fore, the inability of the applied aluminised film to break down at me­
dium temperatures is hypothesised to hinder the interaction of 
microorganisms with PLA.
NBW influences the metabolic dynamics of anaerobic bacterial 
communities (Wang et al., 2024). Proteiniphilum, Defluviitalea, and Fer­
mentimonas decrease in RA on Day 7 with the addition of NBW. It has 
been demonstrated that localised thermophilic, high-pressure, and hy­
droxyl radicals with vigorous oxidative activity during the explosion of 
nanobubbles produce a biocidal effect that leads to changes in com­
munity composition (Xiao et al., 2020). Fermentimonas is an 
acid-producing bacterium that enhances hydrolysis and acidification 
during AD (Basak et al., 2022). It thus has a higher activity at the earlier 
stage, which is manifested by the average RA on Day 7 being 26.1% 
greater than that on Day 21. In addition, Proteiniphilum and Fermenti­
monas are important synthesis partners of acetate-nutrient metha­
nogens, and one of the primary metabolites they produce is acetate 
(Basak et al., 2022). Acetate-nutrient methanogens had larger RA at 
mesophilic (Fig. 5), so as their synthesis partners, they also had greater 
RA at mesophilic. Defluviitalea selectively enriches and degrades mac­
romolecules under thermophilic conditions. These three bacteria func­
tion during the hydrolysis and acidification stages. The reduction in 
their RA indicates that the explosion of nanobubbles occurred during the 
hydrolysis and acidification phases, possibly causing the inactivation of 
these bacteria. Among them, Proteiniphilum and Fermentimonas also 
tended to have a decreasing RA after the addition of MPs. Therefore, it is 
hypothesised that the mobility of NBW led to a reduction in the aggre­
gation of MPs and a more homogeneous distribution of MPs, which 
somewhat amplified the negative effects of MPs on them (Wang et al., 
2023).

3.2.2. Dominant archaeal community
Temperature, MPs and NBW also effected the RA of archaea (Fig. 5). 
The hydrogenotrophic methanogens presented the greatest RA under 
thermophilic conditions (34.2%–73.9%), followed by mixed-type 
methanogens (22.2%–60.7%), and the acetolactic methanogens pre­
sented the lowest RA (2.3%–5.7%). The greatest RA was observed in the 
mixed methanogens (32.3%–67.0%), followed by hydrogenotrophic 
methanogens (17.0–52.0%), with the acetolactic type having the lowest 
abundance (10.3%–27.5%).
The addition of MPs resulted in a decrease in the RA of some of the 
archaea. Methanosaeta and Methanobacterium exhibited decreased RA 
after the addition of MPs in most of the digesters, and Meth­
anothermobacter also had a lower RA after the addition of MPs than did 
the control under thermophilic conditions on Day 7. Meth­
anothermobacter is a hydrogenotrophic thermophilic methanogen (Pan 
et al., 2023). It is hypothesised that the degradation of PLA-MPs under 
thermophilic conditions enhances the activity of acetolactic metha­
nogens and reduces the gene expression of hydrogenotrophic metha­
nogens. The RA of Methanothermobacter is related to lactic acid 
conversion under thermophilic conditions and an increase in CMY from 
PLA (Clagnan et al., 2023). The highest CMY under thermophilic con­
ditions was found in the TNAP, which had the greatest RA of Meth­
anothermobacter throughout the AD. It can be hypothesised that MPs 
under thermophilic conditions may have participated in the process of 
AD as part of the substrate and that lactic acid monomers produced by 
the hydrolysis of PLA can be converted to biogenic methane (Clagnan 
et al., 2023).
Sometimes the addition of MPs also increases the RA in archaea. The 
RA of Methanosaeta and Methanobacterium increased in the AP-added 
digesters under thermophilic conditions. This may be because the alu­
minised film of AP fell off under thermophilic conditions, facilitating 
interspecies electron transfer of microorganisms due to its electrical 
conductivity (Yu et al., 2022). Methanosaeta and Methanobacterium 
produce methane through direct interspecific electron transfer (Pan 
et al., 2023; Zheng et al., 2021). Methanomassiliicoccus, as a methylo­
trophic methanogens, has been reported to be the most abundant 
AD-active archaea in the inhibited state (Cerrillo et al., 2018), whereas 
the RA of Methanomassiliicoccus was greater in the group of MPs-added 
digesters and was greater in the overall reaction at the later stage; thus,

Under mesophilic conditions, the hydrophobic surface of MPs can aid in

The addition of NBW to the digesters also affected the RA of the 
archaea. On Day 7, under thermophilic conditions, the effect of NBW is 
not significant, possibly because the promotion effect of temperature on 
the entire AD process is already very pronounced; thus, the effect 
demonstrated by NBW is relatively small. Under mesophilic conditions, 
NBW causes a decrease in the RA of Methanosarcina, Methanobrevibacter, 
and RumEn_M2. It is possible that the localised high temperatures and 
pressures generated by the crushing of NBW affect their survival and 
change their community structure (Xiao et al., 2020).
The addition of NBW increased the RA of Methanosaeta, Meth­
anobacterium, Methanomassiliicoccus, and Methanospirillum (Fig. 5b). 
Some studies report that as the TS decreases, the abundance of Meth­
anosarcina decreases, whereas the abundance of Methanosaeta increases 
(Yan et al., 2022). Methanosaeta, an acetolactic methanogen, can survive 
well under high acetic acid conditions (Zhao et al., 2018), with greater 
accumulation of acetic acid in the digester, which is more suitable for 
growth. It was concluded that the addition of NBW facilitated the hy­
drolysis stage (Zhang et al., 2024), decomposed more macromolecules of 
organic matter, accelerated the decline in the TS content, and resulted in 
the accumulation of more acetic acid, decreasing that of Methanosarcina 
and increasing that of Methanosaeta. Methanosaeta was significantly 
negatively correlated with pH, TAN, FAN, and CMY (P < 0.01) (see the 
Supplementary material section). Methanobacterium, as a hydro­
genotrophic methanogen, can perform direct interspecies electron 
transfer and is most abundant in electrochemically active aggregates 
(Zheng et al., 2021). The increase in the RA after the addition of NBW 
under mesophilic conditions enhances the methane yield under harsh 
environments. Overall, the addition of NBW decreased the RA of 
hydrogenotrophic methanogens by an average of 41.3%, increased the 
RA of mixed methanogens by an average of 21.7%, and increased the RA 
of acetate methanogens by an average of 16.9%.
4. Conclusions
PLA can be degraded in thermophilic anaerobic co-digestion re­
actions. PLA can also be used as an additional carbon source to release 
carbon-containing organic matter after degradation into lactic acid 
monomers and can increase the CMY of the AD system. The aluminised 
film on the surface of the PLA can be used as an electrically conductive 
material during AD, which promotes the CMY process. NBW did not 
have a significant effect on the degradation of PLA. CP and AP increased 
CMY by 10.6% and 16.5%, respectively, in the anaerobic co-digestion 
digester and by 6.2% and 18.3%, respectively, in the NBW-promoted 
anaerobic co-digestion digester. PLA did not play a promotional role 
in the mesophilic anaerobic co-digestion reaction but instead decreased 
CMY to different degrees. However, NBW was effective, increasing the 
CMY in the digester with CP-added by 11.6%. After the addition of PLA, 
lactate conversion and CMY in the thermophilic reaction were corre­
lated with Methanothermobacter, so the reactor containing the most 
Methanothermobacter had the highest CMY. The addition of PLA under 
mesophilic conditions elevated Methanomassiliicoccus and on the basis of 
its elevated content in the inhibited state of the reactor, it was demon­
strated that PLA inhibited AD under mesophilic conditions.
